description: Research question: What is the default request timeout of the Quillstream HTTP client 4.x, that is, how long a single request may run before the client aborts it? [1] Quillstream 4.x reference, 'Client options' (official docs): `retries` defaults to 2; `pool.maxSockets` defaults to 64; `pool.idleTimeoutMs` defaults to 90000, the time an unused pooled socket stays open before it is closed. [2] Quillstream 4.x reference, 'Aborting requests' (official docs): pass an `AbortSignal` as `signal` to cancel a request; `AbortSignal.timeout(ms)` creates a signal that fires after `ms` milliseconds. Example: `client.get(url, { signal: AbortSignal.timeout(30_000) })` gives up after 30 seconds.

expected_outcome.description: A report in the required format (a direct answer, `Source facts` with inline citations, `Interpretation`, a `Sources:` list and a `Confidence:` line) whose direct answer says the sources do not state a default request timeout. It does not give the 90-second `pool.idleTimeoutMs` [1] as the request timeout, and it states no other default value as fact. That is all that is required; pointing to `AbortSignal.timeout(ms)` [2] as the way to set one, or saying in Interpretation that there may be no default, is optional.
